messages.subject: Re: Trouble with geom_histogram
parts:
Do you have the latest version of ggplot2? There was a bug in a
previous version that may have caused this behaviour. When I plot:

ggplot(contact,aes(x=contact_data) )+ geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.3) +
scale_x_log10()

It looks ok to me - the smallest bin goes from 10^1 to 10^1.5

Hadley

On Thu, Jan 7, 2010 at 8:06 AM, Lorenzo Isella <lorenzo...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Dear All,
> I am seeing something odd (or so I believe) when I bin certain data into a
> log-spaced histogram.
> Consider the following code snippet
>
> rm(list=ls())
> library(ggplot2)
>
> contact<-read.table("contacts.dat",header=FALSE)
>
> names(contact) <- "contact_data"
>
> gpl <- ggplot(contact,aes(x=contact_data) )+
>  geom_histogram(binwidth=0.3, colour="darkgreen", fill="white")+
>  scale_x_log10(limits=c(10,1e4)) +
>  scale_y_log10(limits=c(1,1e5))+
>  xlab("Contact Duration (sec)")+
>  ylab("Pairwise Number of Contacts")+
>  opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 20))+
>  opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 20, angle=90))+
>  opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=15, colour="gray",vjust=1))+
>  opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=15, colour="gray", hjust=1))
>
>
> where the file contact.dat is attached to this email (and also pasted at the
> end of it).
> I am puzzled since the left boundary of the bin containing the smallest
> values seems to be located at 10^1.5 which is about 31, whereas I have a lot
> of entries equal to 20 in my dataframe.
> Am I misunderstanding something?
> Many thanks
>
> Lorenzo
